hints: Focus on what the backbone of an addition polymer looks like, with each C=C carbon becoming a single-bonded CH unit in the chain.
Draw but-2-ene as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ and notice each double-bond carbon already has one H and one $\text{CH}_3$ group.
Open the double bond to form single bonds to neighbours and check that every chain carbon keeps its H and its methyl group.
walkthrough:
**Picture what addition polymerisation does**

Think of the C=C double bond opening up. Each alkene molecule adds on, so the two C atoms from the double bond become two new single-bonded carbons in the long chain.

$$ \text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{-C-C-} $$

**Translate the description of polymer G**

Every carbon in the chain has one H and one methyl group. That means the repeat pattern must be:

$$ \text{-[CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CH}_3\text{)]-}_n $$
So we need an alkene where both C=C carbons each carry one H and one $\text{CH}_3$.

**Test but-2-ene**

But-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$. Look at the left C: bonded to H and $\text{CH}_3$. Look at the right C: bonded to H and $\text{CH}_3$. Perfect match.

$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 \rightarrow \text{-[CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CH}_3\text{)]-}_n $$
This gives exactly polymer G.

options.A: But-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It polymerises to $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)]-}_n$. One chain carbon has two H atoms and the other has an ethyl group, not a methyl on every carbon.
options.B: But-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$. Both alkene carbons have one H and one $\text{CH}_3$. On polymerisation the double bond opens to give $\text{-[CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CH}_3\text{)]-}_n$, so every backbone carbon has one H and one methyl group.
options.C: Methylpropene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. It gives $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]-}_n$. One carbon has two H atoms and the other has two methyl groups and no H, so it does not fit the one H plus one methyl rule.
options.D: Propene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_3$. It gives poly(propene), $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)]-}_n$. Only alternate carbons carry a methyl group, while the $\text{CH}_2$ carbons carry two H atoms. This is a common trap if you only check one carbon.
